intro: Searching for an employment solicitor near you usually means something at work has reached the point where you want proper legal guidance rather than a colleague's opinion. You might be facing a dismissal, a redundancy process, or a settlement agreement you have been asked to sign. We can introduce you to a UK employment solicitor in your area who will quote you directly, with the price on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an employment solicitor near you usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for an employment solicitor near them are dealing with a live problem at work and want to understand their options before deciding what to do next.
needs: You have been dismissed and want to know whether the way it was handled was fair, and what you could do about it.
You are being offered a settlement agreement and have been told you need independent legal advice before signing.
You believe you have been treated unfairly because of a protected characteristic such as age, sex, disability or race, and want to understand whether that amounts to discrimination.
You are in a redundancy consultation and want to know how the process should work and what your entitlements are.
You are still employed but facing a disciplinary or grievance process and want advice on how to handle it.
context: Employment tribunal time limits are short. For most claims the deadline is often three months less a day from the date of the act you are complaining about, so it is worth getting advice early rather than waiting.

Before most tribunal claims can proceed, you usually need to go through ACAS early conciliation. An employment solicitor can explain how this fits with your deadline and what happens during the process.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Describe the situation at work in your own words, including what has happened and when.
Say whether you are still employed or your employment has ended, and on what date.
Mention any dates that matter, such as a deadline in a settlement agreement or a date you were dismissed.
Explain whether you have already raised a grievance or started ACAS early conciliation.
Say where you are based so we can introduce you to a solicitor near you.
Note anything you particularly want help with, such as reviewing a document or advice on next steps.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the employment solicitor
questions: Are you regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority, and can you confirm your firm's register entry?
How will you charge for this matter, and can you give me a sense of the likely cost before we start?
What is my deadline for bringing a claim, and does ACAS early conciliation change it?
Will you handle my matter personally, or will someone else in the firm do the work?
What do you need from me to get started, and how quickly can we speak?
If I have a settlement agreement, can you advise me independently on its terms?

faqs.q: Do I need a solicitor who is near me physically?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, as much employment advice can be given by phone or video. But searching for an employment solicitor near you can be useful if you would prefer to meet in person or deal with a firm you can visit.

faqs.q: How do I check that an employment solicitor is properly regulated?
faqs.a: Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority, and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland the regulator is the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland it is the Law Society of Northern Ireland.

faqs.q: I have been asked to sign a settlement agreement. What should I do?
faqs.a: Settlement agreements need independent legal advice before you sign, so it is worth speaking to an employment solicitor promptly. They can explain the terms and what you are agreeing to, and the price will be quoted to you directly.

faqs.q: How soon should I contact an employment solicitor?
faqs.a: Employment tribunal time limits are short, often three months less a day, and ACAS early conciliation usually has to happen first. Getting advice early gives you more room to consider your options.

extra_heading: Choosing between employment solicitors near you
extra: Searching for an employment solicitor near you often means you want someone you could actually sit down with, perhaps because the situation feels personal or because you would rather not explain it all over the phone to a stranger. It is worth thinking about what matters most to you before you start ringing round: a firm you can reach easily, someone who deals with the employee side of workplace disputes, or a solicitor who can see you quickly because a deadline is looming.

Employment law sits on both sides of the fence, so ask whether the solicitor mainly acts for employees or for employers. A firm that usually advises employers may still be able to help you, but you will want to feel confident they understand your position. When you speak to them, ask how they would approach your particular situation and whether they have handled matters like yours before, so you can judge for yourself rather than relying on any label.

It also helps to compare more than one option. You can check each solicitor or firm on the Solicitors Regulation Authority's register if you are in England or Wales, or the relevant Law Society in Scotland or Northern Ireland, and ask each one how they charge and what they would need from you. We introduce you to a suitable UK employment solicitor near you who will quote you directly, with the price on application, so you can weigh up the options and decide what suits you.

extra_faqs.q: Will the solicitor near me act for me or for my employer?
extra_faqs.a: Employment solicitors can act for either employees or employers, and some firms do both. It is worth asking directly who they usually represent, so you can decide whether they are the right fit for your situation.

extra_faqs.q: Can I speak to a solicitor near me before deciding whether to instruct them?
extra_faqs.a: Many firms will talk to you briefly about your situation before you commit, though some may charge for a longer appointment. Ask when you enquire what the first conversation involves and how any charge will work, with the price on application.

extra_faqs.q: What if there is no employment solicitor in my own town?
extra_faqs.a: You may still be able to get advice from a solicitor further away by phone or video, and searching near you can simply be a starting point. If meeting in person matters to you, say so when you enquire and we can take that into account when introducing you.
